title: You are having a panic attack
lede: Your heart is hammering, your hands are numb, your chest is tight, and you are certain something is very wrong. You may be in a meeting, a supermarket, a train, or your own kitchen.

blocks.text: Your heart is hammering, your hands are numb, your chest is tight, and you are certain something is very wrong. You may be in a meeting, a supermarket, a train, or your own kitchen.

items: The sensations are real, the danger is not. Panic is an alarm system firing in the absence of the thing it evolved to detect.
The tingling hands and light head come from over-breathing, which lowers carbon dioxide. That is why slowing the out-breath specifically helps, rather than deep breaths in.
A panic attack peaks in roughly ten minutes and then falls, whatever you do. Knowing there is a ceiling is itself calming.
Fighting it makes it longer. The paradox is that allowing the sensations shortens the episode.

items.move: Slow the out-breath, not the in-breath
items.detail: In for four, out for seven or eight, through the mouth. Longer exhale than inhale, repeated. This is the physiological lever.

items.move: Put your feet flat and press them down
items.detail: Weight through the soles, hands on a solid surface. Physical contact interrupts the disembodied feeling.

items.move: Name five things you can see, out loud if possible
items.detail: It occupies the part of the brain currently generating catastrophe.

items.move: Say what it is, to yourself, plainly
items.detail: "This is panic. It peaks and it passes. I am not in danger."
Cold water on the wrists or the back of the neck triggers a genuine calming reflex.

items.move: Stay where you are if it is safe to
items.detail: Fleeing works instantly and teaches your brain the place was dangerous. Staying is what shrinks it long term.

items.say: "My body is doing panic. It is uncomfortable and it is not dangerous. It will peak and drop."
"I am having a panic attack. I am fine, I do not need an ambulance, I just need five minutes and some air."
"Do not ask me questions. Just breathe slowly with me and stay."

items.when: If you must leave a room
items.say: "Give me ten minutes and I will be back." Naming the return matters.

items: Big fast deep breaths. It worsens the over-breathing and prolongs the symptoms.
Alcohol, energy drinks, or extra caffeine.
Repeatedly checking your pulse. It feeds the loop directly.
Building a permanent avoidance around the place it happened. Avoidance is what turns one attack into a shrinking life.
Deciding you are broken. This happens to an enormous number of people and responds very well to treatment.
Eat and drink something. Blood sugar and dehydration lower the threshold for the next one.
Write down what preceded it: sleep, caffeine, conflict, deadline, skipped meals. Patterns appear within weeks.
Return to the same place soon and do something small and ordinary there.
If it recurs, see a doctor and ask specifically about CBT for panic. It has a strong evidence base and it is time-limited.

limit: If it is your first episode, or there is crushing chest pain, pain spreading to the arm or jaw, or you are short of breath at rest, treat it as a possible cardiac event and get emergency medical help. Do not diagnose panic on a first occurrence.
